newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Serb acquitted in first Swiss war crimes trial.
newsitem.headline: Serb acquitted in first Swiss war crimes trial.

text.p: A Bosnian Serb accused of murder and torture at wartime detention camps was acquitted on Friday by a military tribunal and awarded 100,000 Swiss francs ($68,500) from the state in damages.
At the end of the country's first-ever war crimes trial, the court ordered Goran Grabez, 32, from the Bosnian town of Prijedor to be freed immediately and compensated him for his period in custody.

The ruling, after a five-day trial, said the prosecutor had failed to prove Grabez had served in July 1992 in the Serb-run Omarska and Keretrem camps in northwestern Bosnia where he was alleged to have beaten and killed Moslem prisoners.

Testimony from witnesses, including fellow asylum-seekers at a Geneva centre where he was arrested in April 1995 after they said they recognised him as a camp guard, was too imprecise, the court found.

Several accounts confused him with another man known as "Karlica", also from the Prijedor region near Banja Luka in northwestern Bosnia and who had been killed in fighting in June 1992, the ruling said.
On the second day of the trial on Tuesday, two witnesses told the court the defendant was one of the Bosnian Serb guards at Omarska.
One of them, a Bosnian Moslem, said he saw Grabez carrying a truncheon go into a house used by Serbs for torture.

The military prosecutor had sought a four-year sentence for Grabez, a driver, who could have faced up to 20 years in jail under the Swiss military penal code if found guilty. He denied the charges, saying he was in Austria and Germany at the time.

The court ordered the Swiss state to pay him 70,000 Swiss francs for "moral injury," on the grounds that his rights had been prejudiced by the war crime accusations, as well as 30,000 francs for lost earnings.
The fees of his defence lawyer are also to be paid by the state, under the ruling.
Both the prosecution and the defence have five days to appeal against the verdict. The prosecutor can challenge the ruling while Grabez can seeker higher damages. ($ = 1.458 Swiss Francs)
